aliases: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
topics.summary: On November 20, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis as a 17-million-line Lean library, made working with Claude, and the Lean and Mathlib communities certified it as correct the next day.
topics.why_now: Two attempts landed the same day: Alpöge's machine-checked proof, and a 940-page human-written manuscript by Alessandro Masullo aimed at the generalized hypothesis, which readers have since found gaps in. The Hacker News thread on Masullo's announcement drew 2,447 points.

topics.name: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini
topics.summary: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights model Thinking Machines Lab released on November 20 under the Apache 2.0 license: a 26.4B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3.4B active, built to run on local hardware such as Macs with 32 GB or more.
topics.why_now: A Hacker News post titled "Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory" drew 582 points. That 5.4 GB figure belongs to an independent compressed build, not the official release, whose checkpoint is about 20 GB.

editorial.brief: Grand Theft Auto VI turned up in two separate clusters, across Google Trends, YouTube and Hacker News, and placed second on Wikipedia with 308,867 views. The Riemann hypothesis also crossed three feeds. Ramayana: Part 1 led Wikipedia with 384,249 views, and no other feed says why.
editorial.cover_sub: Ramayana: Part 1 drew 384,249 views, 1.2 times the runner-up, while the other feeds spent the day on a video game, a mathematics problem and Christmas playlists.
editorial.wiki_deck: Ramayana: Part 1 took the top Wikipedia spot with 384,249 views. No other feed in the snapshot mentions it, so the crowd arrived without leaving a trail.
editorial.letter_headline: A day of games, proofs and playlists
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News tinkers with old video archives, XNU on Linux and local AI, while Lemmy is irritated by politics and power plants. Bluesky collects poems and postcards, and Mastodon posts cats and paintings.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire followed the Anthropic IPO and doubts about the AI boom, while Americans searched for soccer standings, king tides, earthquakes and the Dow.
editorial.markets_deck: Today's markets are long shots and settled questions: a ceasefire at 100 percent, Shakhtar's Champions League hopes at 0, Jensen Huang's NVIDIA return at 3. Volume reads $0M throughout.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaks at 1,226,352 players on Steam, ahead of Dota 2 at 888,569 and PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS at 771,537. On Twitch, caseoh_ has 78,613 viewers and xQc has 30,411.
editorial.yt_note: A Christmas playlist leads with 556,283 views, with an episode of Can Em All close behind at 504,696. The Avengers: Doomsday update has 26,310, and SANDAUN LEWA has 18,748.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow the Ramayana: Part 1 lead will have moved on, along with the king tides, the earthquake searches and a 3 percent chance of Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA. The GTA 6 mission list and the Christmas playlist may linger. Cyberleek, whatever it is, probably will not.
wiki_paras: Ramayana: Part 1 was the most-read article on Wikipedia in this snapshot, with 384,249 views. Grand Theft Auto VI followed on 308,867, and the 1951-born American football subject Tom Jackson took third with 263,973. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and the Riemann hypothesis completed the top five.

The margin was modest. Ramayana: Part 1 beat the runner-up by 75,382 views, a ratio of 1.2 to one. That is a lead, not a landslide, and the top five sit within a factor of two of each other. Fifth place, the Riemann hypothesis, trailed the leader by 178,456 views.

Nothing else in the snapshot accounts for it. Ramayana appears on no social feed, no search list and no market, so the readers came from somewhere the other feeds do not look. The day's cross-feed stories belonged to GTA 6 and the Riemann hypothesis, both of which sat lower on this list.
letter_paras: The snapshot found a scattered day with two loud corners. Grand Theft Auto VI surfaced in two clusters, one on Google Trends and YouTube about the chapter 2 mission list, one on Hacker News and YouTube about the birds of Vice City. The Riemann hypothesis crossed Hacker News, Polymarket and Wikipedia. Everything else stayed in its own feed.

Some of the smaller entries deserve a look. Hugging Face lists inworld/voice-isolator at 0 downloads, while unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF has 805,993. Cloudflare's top five domains are the usual infrastructure, with google.com first. On Polymarket, an Israel and Iran ceasefire question sits at 100 percent yes, and a Shakhtar Donetsk Champions League bet at 0.

A same-hour snapshot is useful because a feed read alone tells you what one crowd wants, and a feed read beside sixteen others tells you whether anyone else agrees. Ramayana: Part 1 led Wikipedia and appeared nowhere else, which is a finding only a comparison can make. The edition is a record of coincidence and its absence.
